extraction.NOTES: Application for patent in fee covering Northwest quarter of Section Three, Township Twenty-Eight, North of Range Seventy-four West of the Fifth Principal Meridian, South Dakota, containing One Hundred and fifty-nine and fifteen-hundredths acres; degree of blood: one-fourth; married; husband has 175 acres, is a citizen and has a patent in fee to his land, is a member of the Standing Rock Sioux Indians, South Dakota; no inherited land; no individual Indian money on credit; not in debt; no other occupation stated beyond housewife; land not leased; no contract to sell land; no one asked her to procure patent for disposing of land; no other trust lands remaining after application is released | SUBSTANTIVE CORRECTION 2026-04-29: BLM accession 716639 (Serial Patent, South Dakota, 11/5/1919, Tribe = Rosebud Sioux) confirms canonical record details. Four Sonnet text-extraction errors corrected: (1) Name 'Ann Black' is OCR misread of 'Anna Blackbird' — Sonnet dropped 'bird' suffix and truncated 'Anna' to 'Ann'; (2) Allotment number 3518 corrected to 6475 — the form had '35918' written in the allotment field but that is a patent reference number, not the allotment; BLM confirms allotment is 6475; (3) Document type corrected to Form 5-105 Application for Patent in Fee (Act of May 8, 1906, 34 Stat. 182) — was misclassified as 'questionnaire'; (4) Tribe added: 'Rosebud Sioux' per BLM. Original NOTES had identified her HUSBAND as Standing Rock Sioux; Anna herself is Rosebud. | RELATIONAL CORPUS DATA: Anna Blackbird appears in three distinct corpus records that together form a documentary thread. Her 1918 Form 5-105 application (this record), and two records of a Feb 5, 1929 letter from Rosebud Superintendent E. E. McKean to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs (part1_agency_narrative_page046 and page049) inquiring whether the Office wanted Circular 2464 information collected for her case. The 1918→1929 thread illustrates the kind of biographical trace that becomes visible only when Name + Allotment + Tribe are normalized across the corpus.
